prompt:
A wide 4:1 landscape picture, a side-view effect, a mechanical part of the metal Keeper, a clockwork owl, breaking apart, for a 2D game, painted as four animation stages of one effect that float side by side on open, empty green. Only the effect is painted; whatever it touches or comes from stays off the canvas. The four stages share one horizontal centre line, centred at one eighth, three eighths, five eighths and seven eighths of the picture width, with the same wide band of empty green around each, so every stage sits alone in the open and none comes near another or the picture edge. Everything is drawn in flat side view with no perspective, at the size of a game sprite; the longest stage spans about a fifth of the picture width.

A gear and spring assembly shatters. Stage 1: a toothed dark iron gear with bronze edges, a hard crack across it and a flash of cream light along the crack. Stage 2: the gear splitting in two, a spring uncoiling, fragments and teeth flying outward, sharp angular amber sparks. Stage 3: the gear in many separate angular iron and bronze fragments scattered in a wide ring, a coil spring pinging loose, spark streaks, and a puff of smoke painted as dark angular ink wash. Stage 4: only a few small drifting fragments, a few dim sparks and faint dark ink-wash smoke, the faintest stage. The fragments are clean metal pieces. The palette is pale cream #FFF5DC for flashes, amber #F5AA28 for sparks, deep bronze #94611E and dark iron grey-brown #3A3328 for the metal, with a near-black ink edge. The metal is dark, worn iron and bronze with thin bronze highlights on its upper edges; bright gold belongs to Ella's magic and is left out. Shapes are angular, faceted cut metal.

Style: a dark painterly etched storybook illustration, ink and wash with fine etched cross-hatching and a faint paper grain inside the shapes only. Large shapes have a clean near-black ink outline #171614 about 2 px wide at this size; hair-thin streaks and tiny sparks carry a hairline ink edge so they keep their colour. One light source sits in front and slightly above: upper edges brighter, lower edges shaded with fine hatching. The glow stays inside each shape, brightest at the core and fading toward the ink outline. The background is one perfectly flat, even, pure green #00FF00 from edge to edge, the shapes cut cleanly against it, and the shapes themselves use only the palette above. The canvas holds only the four effects floating on the green, as a clean sprite strip with nothing else on it.
